blogPosts.title: How Much Does Frameless Shower Screen Installation Cost in Moorabbin?
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the real costs of frameless shower screen installation in Moorabbin, including pricing factors, glass types, and how to get the best deal from your local glazier.
body: If you are renovating your bathroom in Moorabbin and considering a frameless shower screen, understanding the costs involved is essential before you commit. Frameless shower screens have become one of the most popular bathroom upgrades across Melbourne's south-east, offering a sleek, modern look that makes even small bathrooms feel open and spacious. At Foley Glass, we install shower screens daily across Moorabbin and surrounding suburbs, so we know exactly what affects the final price.

The cost of a frameless shower screen in Moorabbin typically ranges from $800 to $2,500 depending on several key factors. The size of the screen is the biggest driver — a standard 900mm panel will cost significantly less than a large 1200mm or 1500mm enclosure. Glass thickness also plays a major role, with 6mm glass being the budget-friendly option while 10mm and 12mm tempered glass offers superior strength and a more premium feel. The type of hinge, handle, and seal you choose can add to the total as well.

Your bathroom layout will also influence the price. A straightforward alcove shower with two fixed panels is more affordable than a corner entry or neo-angle configuration that requires custom-cut glass and additional hardware. If your walls are not perfectly plumb — which is common in older Moorabbin homes — your glazier may need to allow for adjustments, which can add a small amount to the quote. This is why an on-site measurement from a qualified glazier like Foley Glass is always recommended before ordering.

When comparing quotes in Moorabbin, make sure you are comparing apples with apples. Some glaziers quote for 6mm glass while others include 10mm as standard. Ask whether the price includes supply and installation, silicone sealing, and cleanup. At Foley Glass, our quotes are all-inclusive so there are no surprises on installation day. We also use Australian-tempered safety glass that meets AS/NZS 1288 standards, ensuring your screen is both beautiful and compliant.

Another factor to consider is the timeframe. Custom frameless shower screens in Moorabbin typically take two to three weeks from measurement to installation. This includes templating, manufacturing, and scheduling the install. If you are on a tight renovation timeline, it pays to get your glazier involved early. Foley Glass can coordinate with your builder or plumber to make sure everything lines up smoothly and your bathroom is finished on schedule.

For Moorabbin homeowners looking for value without compromising quality, we recommend starting with a free on-site quote from Foley Glass. We will measure your space, discuss glass options, and provide a fixed price that covers everything. Whether you want a minimalist frameless screen or a semi-frameless option to stretch your budget, our team will help you find the right solution for your bathroom and your bank balance.

blogPosts.title: Glass Pool Fencing in Melbourne's South-East: What Moorabbin Homeowners Need to Know
blogPosts.excerpt: Everything Moorabbin homeowners need to know about glass pool fencing, from Victorian safety regulations and glass types to pricing and choosing a qualified glazier.
body: Installing a pool is one of the best investments a Moorabbin homeowner can make, but before you can enjoy those summer swims, you need compliant pool fencing. In Victoria, pool fencing is not just a safety measure — it is a legal requirement under the Building Act 1993 and the associated regulations. Glass pool fencing has become the preferred choice across Melbourne's south-east because it provides safety without obstructing the view of your pool and garden.

Victorian regulations require pool fencing to be at least 1200mm high, with self-closing and self-latching gates that open away from the pool. The gap between the bottom of the fence and the ground must not exceed 100mm, and the fence must not have any climbable features within 900mm of the top. For glass pool fencing in Moorabbin, this means the panels must be toughened or laminated safety glass that meets AS/NZS 1170 standards. Foley Glass ensures every installation meets these requirements.

The cost of glass pool fencing in Moorabbin varies based on the length of the pool perimeter, the type of glass, and the ground conditions. On average, homeowners can expect to pay between $200 and $350 per linear metre for supply and installation of frameless glass fencing. Semi-frameless options are more affordable, starting from around $150 per linear metre. For a standard 20-metre pool perimeter, you are looking at roughly $4,000 to $7,000 for a fully installed frameless system.

One common mistake Moorabbin homeowners make is choosing the cheapest quote without verifying that the installer is fully qualified and uses certified glass. Non-compliant pool fencing is not just dangerous — it can result in fines from your local council and may void your home insurance. At Foley Glass, all our glaziers are fully qualified and we use only Australian-certified safety glass. We also arrange the final pool safety inspection to make sure your fencing passes on the first go.

The installation timeline for glass pool fencing in Moorabbin is typically one to two weeks from the initial measure. The process involves site assessment, ground preparation, post or spigot installation, glass panel fitting, and gate installation. Ground conditions matter — if your pool surround is sloped or uneven, additional preparation may be needed. Our team at Foley Glass handles everything from start to finish, including any masonry or concrete work required for secure post mounting.

If you are a Moorabbin homeowner planning a pool or upgrading existing pool fencing, start with a free measure and quote from Foley Glass. We will assess your site, recommend the best fencing system for your pool layout and budget, and provide a fixed price with no hidden costs. Our goal is to keep your family safe while giving you a pool area that looks incredible from every angle.

blogPosts.title: Glass Splashbacks vs Tiles: Which Is Better for Your Moorabbin Kitchen?
blogPosts.excerpt: Comparing glass splashbacks and tiles for your Moorabbin kitchen renovation — costs, durability, maintenance, and why more homeowners are making the switch to glass.
body: Choosing between glass splashbacks and tiles is one of the biggest decisions Moorabbin homeowners face during a kitchen renovation. Both options have their merits, but the right choice depends on your budget, style preferences, and how much maintenance you are willing to do. At Foley Glass, we install glass splashbacks across Moorabbin every week, and we have seen a clear shift in recent years as more homeowners choose glass for its sleek appearance and easy upkeep.

Tiles have been the traditional splashback choice in Australian kitchens for decades. They are affordable, widely available, and come in countless designs. However, tiles come with a significant drawback: the grout lines. In a kitchen environment where grease, steam, and food splatter are daily occurrences, grout lines trap dirt and stains over time. Cleaning tile grout is labour-intensive and often requires harsh chemicals. In Moorabbin's humid summer months, mould can also become an issue in poorly sealed grout.

Glass splashbacks eliminate the grout problem entirely. A single sheet of coloured or printed glass creates a seamless, easy-to-clean surface that can be wiped down in seconds. Glass is non-porous, so it does not absorb stains, odours, or bacteria — making it one of the most hygienic splashback options available. For Moorabbin families who spend a lot of time in the kitchen, this practical benefit alone often tips the balance in favour of glass.

When it comes to cost, glass splashbacks in Moorabbin typically range from $400 to $900 per square metre including supply and installation. Basic tile splashbacks can be cheaper at $100 to $300 per square metre, but once you factor in the cost of tiling labour, grout, and sealing, the gap narrows considerably. Glass also offers long-term value because it does not degrade, discolour, or need re-sealing over time. Many Moorabbin homeowners find that glass splashbacks last the lifetime of the kitchen.

Design flexibility is another area where glass excels. Modern glass splashbacks are available in virtually any colour, and high-definition printed designs can replicate the look of marble, timber, or stone without the maintenance headaches. At Foley Glass, we help Moorabbin homeowners choose splashback colours and finishes that complement their benchtops, cabinetry, and overall kitchen design. We can also install LED backlighting behind glass splashbacks for a stunning ambient effect.

For Moorabbin homeowners weighing up their splashback options, we recommend getting a free quote from Foley Glass to compare the true cost of glass versus tiles for your specific kitchen. We will measure your splashback area, show you our colour range, and provide a fixed price for supply and installation. Most splashback projects in Moorabbin are completed in just one to two days, meaning minimal disruption to your household during the renovation.

blogPosts.title: When to Replace Your Windows: A Guide for Moorabbin Homeowners
blogPosts.excerpt: Learn the warning signs that your Moorabbin home needs new windows, from drafts and condensation to rising energy bills, and how to choose the right replacement glass.
body: Windows are one of the most important features of any Moorabbin home, but they are often overlooked until a serious problem develops. Over time, window glass and seals deteriorate, leading to drafts, condensation, reduced energy efficiency, and even security risks. Knowing when to repair and when to replace your windows can save Moorabbin homeowners thousands of dollars in energy costs and prevent more expensive damage down the track.

One of the clearest signs that your windows need attention is condensation between the panes of double-glazed glass. This indicates that the seal has failed and the insulating gas has escaped. Once this happens, the window loses much of its thermal performance and will let in drafts during Moorabbin's chilly winter months. If you notice persistent fogging or water droplets between glass panes, it is time to call a qualified glazier like Foley Glass to assess whether repair or replacement is the best option.

Drafts around window frames are another warning sign. Hold a lit candle or incense stick near the edges of your windows on a windy day — if the flame flickers or the smoke drifts, air is getting through. In older Moorabbin homes, timber frames may have warped or rotted over the years, creating gaps that let in cold air in winter and hot air in summer. Replacing the glass alone may not solve the problem if the frame itself is compromised, so a professional assessment is essential.

Rising energy bills are often linked to poor window performance. According to the Australian Government's energy efficiency guidelines, single-glazed windows can lose up to ten times more heat than a well-insulated wall. For Moorabbin homes still fitted with original single glazing, upgrading to double glazing or low-emissivity glass can dramatically reduce heating and cooling costs. Many Moorabbin homeowners report noticeable reductions in their energy bills within the first winter after upgrading their windows.

Security is another factor worth considering. Older windows with worn locks, thin glass, or weakened frames are easier targets for break-ins. Upgrading to toughened safety glass or laminated glass provides a much stronger barrier against forced entry. Foley Glass supplies and installs security-rated glass options for Moorabbin homes, giving you peace of mind without sacrificing natural light or aesthetics. We can also replace locks and hardware on existing frames where the glass is still in good condition.

If you are a Moorabbin homeowner noticing any of these warning signs, book a free window assessment with Foley Glass. Our qualified glaziers will inspect your windows, identify any issues, and provide honest recommendations on whether repair or replacement is the most cost-effective solution. We handle everything from single pane replacements to full window upgrades, and our fixed quotes mean you will know the exact cost before any work begins.
